title: Packet cards
subject: Computing
source: Seeded from computing/y8 lesson 11 (Packet cards (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 11: Packets and addresses: how data travels. To understand how data is split into packets with IP addresses and routed across the internet

cards:
packet
a small chunk of data with a
header

IP address
a number that identifies a
device on a network

packet switching
packets travel separately and
are reassembled

header
addressing information at the
front of a packet
blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: Packets arrive in the order 3, 1, 4, 2. What does the receiver do?
questions.model: I do: read the packet numbers in the headers and sort them.

questions.q: Unplugged simulation (pupil PDF): split a 12-word sentence into 4 packets with headers, 'route' them in a shuffled order, then reassemble.
questions.a: Correct packets with headers, reassembled in order.
questions.model: The teacher makes packet 1 with its header.

questions.q: what happens if packet 2 never arrives?
is 192.168.300.1 a valid IPv4 address? Why?
Back to our ponder: A large photo is sent as hundreds of small pieces. Why not send it in one piece?
questions.a: Small packets can take the fastest routes, share the network fairly and be resent if lost.
